title.narrative: Capacity of the National Institute of Ecology and Climate (INECC) developed to independently prepare climate change mitigation modelling, integrating energy and transport, including economic, social and environmental co-benefits, to understand impact of different policy actions for Mexico.

Modelling tools applied with focus on sector integration that consider co-benefits.
Scenarios developed to demonstrate low carbon pathways for various sectors, supporting more ambitious climate change mitigation targets and co-benefits impact.
Communication of modelling results to sectors, based on creditable data, that allow authorities in other sectors to apply the results in development of sector policies and plans.

target.value: Progress in implementing annual activities towards the expected final output target.

actual.value: 2-year scenario-based integrated energy system modelling project initiated in 2022, and is largely on track, however with some activities postponed to next year. Results include: -Data is updated - The power sector model is updated, storage has been included and ready for validation -Definition of scenarios is in the making The refinery model is being reviewed -Training for non-modellers completed.

target.value: Modelling tools in place and in a process of being calibrated - Scenarios reflecting short, medium- and long-term goals developed jointly by INECC and SEMARNAT, and consulted among stakeholders -Inform the update of the national strategy on climate change
Progress in implementing annual activities towards the expected final output target.

actual.value: Activities are on track to meet 2025 target indicators.

target.value: Progress in implementing annual activities towards the expected final output target.

actual.value: Activity partly on track because of delays in completion of agreed 2021 activities.

target.value: Advanced use of modelling tools is part of INECCs standard procedures - Additional scenarios include and assess co-benefits, reflecting short, medium- and long-term goals developed jointly by INECC and SEMARNAT and consulted among stakeholders

title.narrative: Ministry of Trade and Industry capacitated to independently prepare high-quality integrated scenario-based long-term modelling of the Vietnamese energy system presented in biennial EORs, to provide significant support to Vietnamese national energy system planning and policy development processes
EOR preparation, independently led by EREA and based on high quality data, develops NDC scenarios that are incorporated into the power planning and policy development

target.value: Progress in implementing annual activities towards the expected mid-term and final output target.

actual.value:
Activity on track according to WP 2021.
However, the launch of the Energy Outlook Report was expected by 2021, however, the launch has been to summer 2022 instead.

target.value: Vietnam Energy Outlook Report is prepared in cooperation between Electricity and Renewable Energy Authority and Danish Energy Agency with significant external support and is used as input to national energy plans.

Vietnam EOR is developed and published, headed by Electricity and Renewable Energy Authority with support from Danish Energy Agency, and used for national energy plans, including the Power Development Plan.
Progress in implementing annual activities towards the expected mid-term and final output target.

actual.value: The goal for EAV to be leading the EOR independently is not realistic. The last year of DEPP III will instead focus on strengthening capacity in bridging short-term security of supply analyses with long-term energy and climate goals.

target.value: Progress in implementing annual activities towards the expected mid-term and final output target.

actual.value: The launch of the Energy Outlook Report 2021 was delayed to June 2022, but the 2023 version is still expected to be finalized at the end of this year. The modeling framework behind the Energy Outlook is used directly for governmental energy planning. But EREA is not heading the development due to lack of time.

target.value: Electricity and Renewable Energy Authority leads, independently, the development of further improved Vietnam Energy Outlook Report and uses it to support national energy plans, including the revision of Power Development Plan with pathways to meet the Nationally Determined Contribution targets.

title.narrative: Decisions by key partners in the Mexican energy sector regarding climate change mitigation pathways and public policy choices, including for potentially raising 2030-ambition level and beyond, is duly informed by integrated scenarios and state-of-the-art tools for modelling, and by enhancing sub-national efforts.
Higher ambition for climate change mitigation set forth by Mexico

target.value: Raising 2030 climate ambition based scenarios and modelling tools

title.narrative: In China, the Energy Research Institute under National Development and Reform Commission provides well informed, coordinated, and data validated information for low carbon energy strategies, targets, policies, and planning at both national and provincial levels by 2025.

Publication of a China Energy Outlook (CEO), providing a low carbon pathway for the entire energy sector, and with coherent national- and provincial-level recommendations supported by the publication of a Provincial Energy Outlook in a relevant province in China

In Vietnam, capacity is enhanced in energy sector planning and policy development, integrating renewable energy, including offshore wind and energy efficiency technologies, as cost-effective measures of meeting the Vietnamese Nationally Determined Contributions while ensuring national security of supply.

Sustainable pathways from developed scenarios with increasing shares of renewable energy, including offshore wind and energy efficient technologies presented in the Energy Outlook Report, are applied within national energy and power planning and policy development.

target.value: EREA leads, independently, the development of further improved Vietnam EOR and uses it to support national energy plans, including the revision of PDP8 with pathways to meet the NDC targets and Well-informed offshore wind regulatory framework scheme prepared.

title.narrative: In South Africa regulatory framework, operational procedures and flexible options in the power system supports cost effective security in supply with a rising share of electricity from renewable energy sources.

1.Recommended amendments, enhancements and actions proposed on technical regulations (grid codes) 2. Percentage reduced curtailment and percentage increased uptake in renewable energy 3. Energy modelling scenarios applied to support the cost-effective integration and expansion of renewable energy
Energy system modelling of the entire energy sector developed, including socioeconomic and sector specific analyses that support the definition of low carbon energy strategies.
ERI produces high-quality bottom-up modelling of the complete energy sector, which forms the basis for policy making and target definition related to the low carbon development of the energy sector.

target.value: Progress in implementing annual activities towards the expected mid-term and final output target.

actual.value: Annual outlook published in May, and extraordinary special report published at COP. Partners have taken increasing ownership of model development following capacity development.

target.value: Progress in implementing annual activities towards the expected mid-term and final output target.

actual.value: On track. ERI is integrat-ing modelling results into daily research, providing policy recommendations for the draft of the 15th five-year plan.

target.value: Energy Research Institutes modelling capability expanded to consider the complete energy sector and carry out socio-economic analyses.
Progress in implementing annual activities towards the expected mid-term and final output target.

actual.value: Satisfactory annual progress with the draft development of the 2021 China Energy Transition Outlook report which was presented at the COP26.

target.value: Energy Research Institutes modelling and analysis of the complete energy sector provides input to the draft of the 15th Five Year Plan.

title.narrative: Capacity building from Danish Energy Agency has resulted in progress of grid codes for increasing renewable energy penetration, changing load patterns for promoting efficient operation of the network.

Recommended amendments and enhancements proposed on technical regulations (grid codes)
Recommended actions taken regarding demand resource connection requirements

target.value: Gap analysis on SO and SDR codes provided guidance on how the gaps need to be addressed and solved 2. Gap analysis on demand resource connection requirements provided guidance on how the gaps need to be addressed and solved.

actual.value: On track but with minor delays due grid codes and license requirements

target.value: Progress in implementing annual activities towards the expected mid-term and final output target.
Progress in implementing annual activities towards the expected mid-term and final output target.

actual.value: Several workshops have been held with the purpose of planning the revision of the relevant system operator and system dispatch grid codes in South Africa to accommodate an increased penetration of renewable energy sources. The focus and interest has increased greatly since the regulator, NERSA, changed the licensing requirements now allowing for smaller renewable energy plants to be constructed quicker.

target.value: Progress in implementing annual activities towards the expected mid-term and final output target.

actual.value: The implementation has not moved as promptly as expected, due to refocus to other grid codes at Eskom due to changed license requirements. DEA can only support them in their processes and have no direct influence over internal processes and priorities in partner organisations. Further, capacity building and training under the Battery Energy Storage Facility Grid Codes were held in 2022. There is currently no work on the demand code.

target.value: Knowledge sharing activities have informed Eskom processes for updating grid codes (including e.g. SO and SDR codes, connection requirements and demand code)
